sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains the error of early idolaters who knew G-d was the ultimate source but mistakenly thought the celestial bodies had free will to channel influence, leading to their worship.

translations.translation: Now, ostensibly it would be possible to explain this based on the known concept
that in the early generations,
those who worshipped the stars and constellations,
knew that the influence that flows into the land through the stars and constellations
(from the precious things of the fruits of the sun and the precious things of the yield of the moons)
is
(not that they themselves influence,
but rather)
that the Holy One, blessed be He, influences through them,
except they erred and thought that the influence that flows from Him, blessed be He, through the stars and constellations is according to their choice,
and they did not know the truth that they have no choice at all,
and they are only like an axe
in the hand of the hewer.
Therefore they prostrated to the stars and constellations and worshipped them,
because according to their error
(that the influence that flows through the stars and constellations is according to their choice)
it is fitting to thank them for this,
like the saying: to the wine, credit goes to its owner.
And also because according to their error that the stars and constellations have free will, they thought that by worshipping them they would influence them more.
And from this there later evolved that they came to a greater error,
that they thought that G-d has abandoned the earth to the hands of the stars and constellations,
and the governance of the earth depends only on them.
And analogous to a king who appointed ministers to govern the state,
for although that which they have the power to govern the state is because the king appointed them over this,
nevertheless,
after they were appointed,
the governance of the state is by the ministers,
and the king does not intervene in this
(except at rare intervals,
for a great need).
[And it can be said,
that this that the nations of the world call Him, blessed be He, by the name "G-d of gods"
includes within it these two types.
For even those who think that G-d has abandoned the earth to the hands of the stars and constellations call Him, blessed be He, by the name "G-d of gods,"
for in addition to this that He, blessed be He, is higher than them and rules over them,
behold, even in this very matter that the stars and constellations are "gods"
(in their opinion),
meaning they have the power to govern the earth and influence in it,
it is not from themselves but because the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them power over this,
analogous to the king's ministers who govern the state because the king appointed them over this.
And on the other hand,
also the error that the influence that flows from the Holy One, blessed be He, through the stars and constellations is according to their choice is included
(in a subtle way)
in "G-d of gods,"
for also this that they can do as they wish
(to influence or not)
is a matter of rulership,
"gods,"
and the negation of the concept of "other gods"
completely is specifically through the knowledge that all intermediaries are only like an axe in the hand of the hewer].
And based on this it would be possible to explain the cleverness of the one who said "I take the king"
(in the allegory),
that this that Israel know the truth that all intermediaries through whom influence comes are only like an axe in the hand of the hewer,
is due to the greatness of their intellect,
that they see the inwardness.
For outwardly it appears
that this that the influence is through the stars and constellations,
is because there is in them an advantage due to which they are fit to be intermediaries,
and this that Israel know that they are only like an axe in the hand of the hewer is due to the greatness of their intellect.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains that the true reason Israel serves only G-d is not merely knowledge, but that they prioritize serving the King over receiving influence, unlike the nations who seek influence without self-nullification.

translations.translation: However, from the fact that the Midrash brings a parable about this from a king and dukes,
even though in the allegory,
the dukes have free will,
therefore it is logical to say that choice regarding the dukes
("I take dukes")
can cause them to influence more to those who chose them
[and unlike in the allegory's meaning,
that worship of the stars and constellations is of no benefit at all,
since they do not have free will],
it is understood,
that this that the clever one said "I take the king" is because serving the king is more important to him than the benefit
(the influence)
that he would have through the ministers.
And from this it is also understood in the allegory's meaning,
that the main reason why the nations of the world worship the sun and moon etc. and Israel do not worship except the Holy One, blessed be He,
is
(not because the nations of the world err that the stars and constellations have free will and Israel know the truth that they are only like an axe in the hand of the hewer,
but rather)
because the nations of the world,
the main thing for them is that they receive the influence,
and for Israel the main thing is to serve the King.
And the concept is,
that the main reason why they worshipped the stars and constellations is
(as explained in the discourses),
because in order to receive influence from holiness one must be in a state of self-nullification,
and since they did not want to nullify themselves,
therefore they worshipped the stars and constellations,
for in order to receive influence from them there is no need for self-nullification,
and as it is brought in the Zohar
that the impure spirit is always available for free and for nothing,
as it is said
"which we ate in Egypt for free,"
for the influence from the other side
(Egypt)
is free.
And there is another reason why they wanted to receive their influence from the stars and constellations,
because also the influence itself
(drawn through the stars and constellations)
is greater.
For since the nourishment of the sitra achra is from the encompassing light that is above the chain of descent,
where the influence from there is not according to calculation,
behold the influence is in great abundance.
And from this is understood the greatness of the praise and cleverness of Israel who do not worship except the Holy One, blessed be He,
for although in order to receive from holiness one needs work and effort,
and even then the influence is
(initially)
in measure and limitation according to the measure of the work,
nevertheless,
they forgo the abundance of influence
(in physicality)
[even though also Israel can receive
(temporarily)
influence from the other side,
and moreover they take the first portion,
nevertheless they forgo this]
and the limited influence drawn from holiness is more beloved to them.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains that the clever one chooses the King because all else changes and is not true existence, while Israel desires influence from holiness even if limited, as it comes from G-d's inner will.

translations.translation: Now, the reason of the clever one
(for the one who chooses the king and not the ministers)
is because "all of them change, but the king does not change."
And ostensibly it would be possible to say the intention in this is,
that the influence that comes from the other side
(even though it is in greater abundance than the influence that comes from holiness)
is a thing that changes and has no permanence.
For after the refinement,
when the sparks that fell into the shells will be refined
(from which is their vitality)
they will be nullified
completely.
[And all the more so regarding Israel,
that even now,
this that Israel can receive vitality from the other side,
is only temporarily].
And so it is on the other side,
that this that the influence that comes from holiness is in measure and limitation,
is only now,
but after the root of the aspect of inwardness will be revealed,
whose root is from the inwardness of the encompassing light,
the influence from holiness will be in a greater abundance than the abundance that flows from the externality of the encompassing light
(which is also relevant to influence in the shells),
as the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
"If for those who transgress His will [it is] so, for those who do His will, how much more so."
But,
this explanation is insufficient,
for according to this,
also the choice of the clever one in the king is for the sake of the influence that he will have through this,
and the difference between him and those who chose the ministers
(dukes etc.)
is that they think only about the present situation,
and the clever one thinks about what will be in the future,
like the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
"Who is wise? One who sees what is born."
But from that which it says in the Midrash,
that this that Israel do not worship except the Holy One, blessed be He, is because "my soul said: 'The L-rd is my portion,'"
it is proven,
that this that the clever one chooses the king is not because of the benefit he will have from this,
but rather because of the king.
And this means that this that Israel choose the Holy One, blessed be He,
even though now the abundance of influence is for those who transgress His will, is
(not because afterwards the influence for those who do His will will be greater,
but rather)
because the influence for those who do His will is from the inwardness of His will, blessed be He, and His true desire,
and the influence for those who transgress His will is like one who throws [something] behind his shoulder to his enemy against his will,
and therefore they specifically want the influence for those who do His will,
even though it is a limited influence,
because it is drawn from the inwardness of His will, blessed be He.
And what it says "all of them change etc.,"
the intention in this is,
that from the fact that they change afterwards it is proven that even now they are not a true existence.
And this that there is in them vitality to give vitality to animals and to the nations of the world,
is not from themselves, G-d forbid, but because they draw from holiness,
and since the vitality of holiness that is in them does not unite with them
(and on the contrary, it is in a state of exile within them),
behold, in terms of their essence they are an aspect of death.
[And likewise is it regarding those who receive the influence of vitality from them,
as explained in Tanya,
that this that the wicked in their lives are called dead
is because their lives are drawn from a place of death and impurity].
And this is "I take the king because all of them change,"
that he does not want influence that is drawn from a place of death and impurity even though it is influence in abundance,
and he specifically wants the influence from the side of holiness even though it is a limited influence.
